# QueryAPIGate

> One governed gate between your databases and everything that asks them for data: saved SQL published as REST endpoints, MCP tools for AI agents, live events and scheduled exports, with identity, grants, parameter validation, masking and an audit record on every call. Self-hosted, Python, Apache-2.0.

Site: https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/
Repository: https://github.com/AnanthaRajuC/QueryAPIGate
Everything below in one file: https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/llms-full.txt

## Glossary

- **Ad-hoc SQL**: SQL a caller sends directly to /execute_sql or the MCP execute_sql tool, rather than a saved query. Only for keys granted a connection, one statement, read-only unless allowed, and confined to allowed_tables. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#ad-hoc-sql)
- **Admin roles**: The four fixed administrator roles: owner (everything), admin (everything but administrators), developer (saved queries and collections, no keys) and auditor (read only, no SQL). (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#admin-roles)
- **Administrator**: A named person or pipeline that manages QueryAPIGate, holding one of four fixed roles and signing in with their own admin tokens, so every change in the audit log has someone behind it. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#administrator)
- **Agent writes**: How an AI agent changes data: only through a saved query its author marked agent_writes, either held for a person’s approval (approval) or as a single idempotent insert (insert). (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#agent-writes)
- **Alerts**: Live conditions worked out on each request, such as key_expiring or writes_awaiting_approval, shown in the Console and at GET /api/v1/alerts, and gone once the cause is. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#alerts)
- **allowed_tables**: A grant that confines a key’s ad-hoc SQL to named tables. The SQL is parsed, not pattern-matched, and a table outside the list answers as if it did not exist. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#allowed-tables)
- **API key**: The credential an application calls with, sent as X-API-Key. Stored only as a SHA-256 hash; it can be scoped, rate-limited, pinned to IP ranges, given an expiry and rotated. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#api-key)
- **Approval (write request)**: A held agent write, wr_…, that an administrator with writes.approve approves or rejects in the Console. Once approved it runs once, for that caller, with exactly the arguments shown, before it expires. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#approval-write-request)
- **Audit log**: The record of every administrative change: who changed what, with the fields that changed. Each entry is chained to the one before, and the log can stream to your SIEM. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#audit-log)
- **Break-glass key**: QUERYAPIGATE_API_KEY: a full-access key that keeps working as an owner when the identity provider is down. Its use raises an alert. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#break-glass-key)
- **Catalogue**: GET /catalog: what the calling key may run, and on what terms, such as whether a query is cached, whether this key may write through it, and its rate limit. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#catalogue)
- **Collection**: A named group of saved queries. A key or role granted a collection reaches every query in it, including ones added later; it can be renamed, exported, imported and handed out as a Postman collection. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#collection)
- **Column masking**: Hiding a column from a caller: hash, mask, null or drop. Traced through aliases, CTEs and joins to the source column; a query whose columns can’t be traced is refused rather than answered unmasked. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#column-masking)
- **Compatibility promise**: What changes only with notice: REST endpoints and responses, CLI commands, environment variables, the storage format, grant fields, the saved-query format, the MCP tool contract and error codes. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#compatibility-promise)
- **Configuration as code**: config export, config diff and config apply: the whole setup as one YAML file with no secret in it, reviewed in a pull request and applied all or nothing. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#configuration-as-code)
- **Connection**: A named database, or a folder or bucket of files, that QueryAPIGate reaches with its own credentials. Callers never see those credentials. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#connection)
- **Console**: The built-in administration UI at /console: connections, saved queries, keys and roles, a SQL editor, history, the audit log, alerts and approvals. Everything it does is also on the Management API. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#console)
- **Data dictionary**: An MCP resource per connection, queryapigate://connections//dictionary, telling an agent what each table and column means and which columns are masked for it. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#data-dictionary)
- **Descriptions**: Plain-language notes on connections, tables, columns and parameters, imported from database comments or written by you, and given to agents and docs alike. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#descriptions)
- **Draft and published**: A saved query has at most one published version: the one /q/ runs and OpenAPI, MCP and Postman describe. Newer versions are drafts, invisible to callers until published. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#draft-and-published)
- **The eight stages**: What every call passes, whichever front door it used: identify the caller, apply its limits, check the grant, validate parameters, guard the SQL, run it, mask and format, record it. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#the-eight-stages)
- **Error code**: The stable code field on every error, such as param_invalid or forbidden. Part of the compatibility promise: an existing code is never renamed or repurposed. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#error-code)
- **Example APIs**: Four worked scenarios installed by queryapigate examples load: reporting, dashboard data, a streaming export and a partner integration, each with a collection, a role and a ready key, removable with one command. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#example-apis)
- **Experimental**: A feature that works but sits outside the compatibility promise until it graduates, labelled wherever you meet it. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#experimental)
- **Export**: queryapigate export or a saved export: a full result written to a file or a bucket through the same streaming path, incrementally from a watermark, with no server needed. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#export)
- **from_claim**: A parameter whose value comes from the caller’s sign-in token instead of the request, so a user can only ever ask for their own rows. A caller who sends it anyway is refused. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#from-claim)
- **Front door**: One of the ways a call arrives: REST, MCP, live events, exports or the Management API. All of them pass the same governance code. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#front-door)
- **Grant**: What a key or role may reach: whole connections, named saved queries or collections, tables for ad-hoc SQL, and which writes, if any. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#grant)
- **Live events**: Server-sent events as saved queries run, per key if you want, from GET /events or the separate queryapigate events server for many clients. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#live-events)
- **Management API**: /api/v1: everything the Console does, over HTTP, for scripts and pipelines. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#management-api)
- **MCP**: The Model Context Protocol, the standard AI agents use to call tools. QueryAPIGate’s MCP server publishes saved queries as tools under the same rules as REST. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#mcp)
- **MCP tool**: A published saved query as an agent sees it: a name, a description, an input schema built from its parameters, and structured results. mcp: false hides a query from MCP while it still serves REST. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#mcp-tool)
- **Parameter rules**: What a :name parameter accepts: type, default, required, enum, numeric range, length and pattern. Values are bound, never spliced into SQL, and a request breaking a rule gets a 400 listing every problem. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#parameter-rules)
- **Quota**: Calls and rows per day or month for a key, with X-Quota-Remaining-* headers on every response and an alert before it runs out. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#quota)
- **Rate limit**: A request budget: a server-wide limit by client address, and an optional per-key rate_limit. A request must pass both; over it, the answer is a 429 with retry_after. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#rate-limit)
- **Request ID**: An identifier on every response, X-Request-Id, also in the error body and on every log line written for that request. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#request-id)
- **Response cache**: Optional HTTP caching a saved query opts into with cache_ttl: ETag, conditional requests and 304, never for a query that writes. In-process, or shared through Redis. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#response-cache)
- **Role**: A reusable template of grants and limits, copied onto a key once when the key is created. Editing or deleting a role later never changes a key made from it. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#role)
- **Run history**: The record of each run: when, which connection, which key, through which front door, how long and how many rows. MCP runs carry "transport": "mcp". (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#run-history)
- **Saved query**: SQL with a name, description, parameters, permissions and optional cache settings, published as GET /q/, an MCP tool and an export from the one definition. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#saved-query)
- **Scoped key**: An API key restricted to a set of connections, an allow-list of saved queries or collections, or both, so it reaches only what it was given. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#scoped-key)
- **Signed-in user**: An app user who calls with their own Authorization: Bearer token from your identity provider instead of a shared key, and is mapped to a role. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#signed-in-user)
- **SQL guard**: The check that lets only single SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE and EXPLAIN statements through by default, before anything reaches the database. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#sql-guard)
- **Store**: Where QueryAPIGate keeps its own state: saved queries, keys, roles, history and the audit log. A SQLite file by default, or PostgreSQL for several instances. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#store)
- **Structured results**: An MCP tool’s answer as data: structuredContent matching its outputSchema, {"rows": [...], "truncated": }, so code reads rows rather than parsing text. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#structured-results)
- **Tier 1**: The database types with every feature, tested against a real server in CI and covered by the compatibility promise. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#tier-1)
- **Workspace**: An experimental way to run several teams on one server, each with its own connections, queries, keys, roles, history and audit entries. Every route also answers at /w//…. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#workspace)
- **Write granularity**: allowed_write_ops: narrowing a key that may write to specific operations, such as only INSERT, or only on one curated query. (https://anantharajuc.github.io/QueryAPIGate-website/Glossary.dc.html#write-granularity)
